Opera today announced that the free built-in VPN in its desktop browser will now automatically activate when users connect to public or unsecured Wi-Fi networks. Read on for details.

The opt-in feature is rolling out today in the US and France first

Opera has offered a free built-in VPN in its browser since 2016. Opera says the feature aligns with its core belief of "making basic online privacy accessible to all."

VPNs have evolved from a relatively niche privacy tool into a mainstream product in recent years. But according to We Are Social's Digital 2026 Half-Year Global Data Report, only 23% of internet users aged 16 and above use a VPN for some of their online activities.

This is a concerning figure, especially for users who rely on public Wi-Fi to work or browse while traveling.

Opera today announced that users in the US and France can opt to have their built-in VPN automatically turn on when connecting to public or unsecured Wi-Fi networks.

Opera said:

Opera emphasized that its "free VPN operates under strict GDPR," noting that the service "has been independently audited by Deloitte." Opera also pointed out that VPN is part of a suite of built-in privacy tools, alongside its native ad blocker and tracker blocker.
